summary: This note is documentation for the SAMPLE / TABLESAMPLE clause, which returns a random subset of rows from a table. It describes two approaches: fraction-based sampling, where each row or block is included with a given probability (BERNOULLI/ROW or SYSTEM/BLOCK), and fixed-size sampling, which returns a specified number of rows (up to 1,000,000). It covers syntax, usage restrictions on seeds, joins, views and subqueries, performance considerations, and examples. SAMPLE and TABLESAMPLE are synonymous.
one_line: Documentation for the SAMPLE/TABLESAMPLE clause, covering fraction-based and fixed-size random row sampling, seeds, and their restrictions.
key_facts: SAMPLE and TABLESAMPLE are synonymous and can be used interchangeably.
The default sampling method is BERNOULLI when no method is specified.
BERNOULLI (or ROW) includes each row with a probability of p/100.
SYSTEM (or BLOCK) includes each block of rows with a probability of p/100 and does not support fixed-size sampling.
The probability can be any decimal number between 0 and 100 inclusive.
The num in num ROWS can be any integer between 0 and 1000000 inclusive.
The seed (REPEATABLE or SEED) can be any integer between 0 and 2147483647 inclusive.
For BERNOULLI or ROW sampling, the expected number of returned rows is (p/100)*n, where n is the number of rows in the table.
Sampling with a seed is not supported on views or subqueries.
Sampling the result of a JOIN is allowed only when the sample is row-based (Bernoulli) and does not use a seed.
SYSTEM and BLOCK sampling are often faster than BERNOULLI or ROW sampling.
Fixed-size sampling can be slower than equivalent fraction-based sampling because it prevents some query optimization.
The example SELECT * FROM testtable SAMPLE (10); returns a sample in which each row has a 10% probability of being included.
